t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone page. Top-left: a large light-weight sans headline in sentence case with a small mono uppercase note set beside its second line. Left 60%: a three-column table with hairline rules, large light row numerals and monospace codes for <CONTENT>. Right 40%: an isometric technical line drawing of a compact process skid with tanks, vessels, pipework and control cabinets on a base frame, uniform navy hairline strokes, white fills, no shading or hatching, isolated. Thin navy strips at the page edges. Square, calm and precise.
signature_idea: A regulatory gap table read beside an isometric catalogue drawing of the skid, with the obsolete-controls warning set as a mono marginal note on the headline.
strengths: marginal mono note beside the headline is a neat, reusable typographic device
large light row numerals and mono clause codes fit the brand exactly
isometric hairline skid is clean and on-style
weaknesses: the drawing does not point to the controls or relate to any row; mostly a table plus picture
skid shows pressure vessels and tank domes that read as stainless rather than PP
invented clause references and PLC model names would be mistaken for facts
navy edge strips are arbitrary framing with no meaning
brand_fit_why: Light headline, mono codes, hairline isometric art, limestone and navy with square corners and space is the brand book almost verbatim.
